note: The cue vocabulary. THE source of truth: engine/stage.js binds handlers to it and refuses to boot with a mismatch, and tools/check-script.py validates chapters against it. This file exists because the list used to be hand-copied between those two, so adding a verb to one and not the other made a typo in a chapter silently do nothing. Arguments are checked too: check-script.py rejects a cue carrying an argument this file does not declare, because `kind` and `tone` sat in the chapter for months being read by nothing and validating clean.

summary.en: Fly the camera to a place

zoom.note: Only meaningful when `places` names exactly one place, where fitting is flying. Ignored otherwise.

summary.en: Set the clock on the map

map.time.note: value: null clears the clock — the epilogue steps outside the day.

region.show.note: Names resolve against the file the chapter declares in `regions`.

vary.note: Give each region its own colour inside the side's family. On by default: thirteen colonies filled with one wash read as one shape, not thirteen. Set false when a shot is about the side and not about the individual areas.

border.set.note: 0 country, 1 state/province. A pack decides what those mean.

strength.note: How many people are moving. A route with a strength draws an army arrow sized by it; a route without one stays a thin line, which is what a single rider or a ship should be. Normally set on the route itself rather than the cue, because it is a fact about who is moving, not about this moment.

route.draw.note: Arrow or line is decided by whether anyone declared a strength — see that argument. Seven hundred regulars and one silversmith must not look alike.

summary.no: En linje som står og venter

front.show.note: Geometry comes from a route, because a line is a line. An arrow says these people moved; a front says they stood there and faced something. Seventy-seven men on a village green are the second thing, and drawing them as an arrow says the one thing about them that is not true.

facing.note: Which side of the line the ticks hang from: 1 or -1. Which way they are looking.

fluid.note: Dashed, for a body of men who have not formed up properly. Most of this chapter.

fit.note: Off by default: a front is usually drawn inside a shot the camera has already framed.

kind.note: point is a plain pin and draws no glyph.

marker.show.note: `kind` decides what happened there, and drops the matching glyph from the map's battle set under the pin. `tone` names a palette colour when the point is not about a side — a bridge people fought over is not a claim about who owns it.

summary.no: Peke på kartet mens du snakker
summary.en: Point at the map while you talk

tone.note: A colour, not a side. Defaults to gold, the map’s "look here" colour.

summary.no: Styrker som kommer inn og møtes

summary.en: A short note under the caption

sound.play.note: A single event: a shot, a bell, a fife. Never replayed when the picture is rebuilt after a seek — scrubbing back through Lexington must not fire forty muskets.

times.note: Fire it this many times, spread over `spread` seconds, each at a slightly different pitch so it reads as several guns rather than one sample stuttering.

summary.en: Lay a bed of place under it

sound.ambience.note: Continuous: wind, sea, a crowd. Crossfades. Omit `id` to stop it.

sound.music.note: Ducks under the voice on its own, from the script word timings. Omit `id` to stop it.

road.draw.note: A standing line, drawn quietly and all at once — not an event. Marches then travel along something instead of across open ground. Takes the same shape as a route, because it IS the route everyone on that day used; drawing it claims no more precision than the marches already do.

summary.no: Gjør et ord i teksten trykkbart
summary.en: Make a word in the caption tappable

term.mark.note: Marks a word so a reader can tap it and read more. Resolved when the chapter is compiled, NOT when the cue fires — the mark is a property of the sentence, not a thing on the stage, so it cannot violate the rule that the picture is a function of time. There is deliberately no `dossier.show`: a cue that OPENED a card would be replayed on every seek, and forty cards would try to open at once. Same reason a musket must not fire forty times when you scrub back through Lexington. term.mark marks; the reader decides whether to look.

kind.note: Which pool the id resolves against.

id.note: Checked against the pool named by `kind`.

span.note: How many words the term covers. 'Second Continental Congress' is a span of three.

summary.no: To eller tre tall som ett bilde
summary.en: Two or three numbers as one picture

compare.show.note: Seventy-seven against seven hundred lands as an argument when it is one picture and as trivia when it is two unrelated chips. Same for 230 ships against 400, and for three shares of the Roman world. `n` sizes the bar; `value` is what is printed. They are separate because the pack writes numbers the way they are SPOKEN in the prose and the way they are READ on screen, and a bar needs neither — it needs a number to measure. A part with no `n` falls back to parsing `value`.

parts.note: Each: { n, value, label, side or tone }.

mode.note: `bar` measures them against the largest. `ratio` sets them side by side as one width.

note.note: One line under the bars, where the comparison needs a caveat.

summary.no: Fyll skjermen med et bilde, og la kameraet gli
summary.en: Fill the screen with a picture, and let the camera drift

plate.show.note: The map is not the only stage. A chapter has moments that are not on a map at all — the Ides of March happens in a room, the will is read in a senate, the Forum is a place you should SEE rather than see a dot for — and until now the only answer was a small inset card over a map that was still the subject of the screen. A plate takes the whole frame, and drifts: the slow push that is the visual grammar of every history documentary ever made, and the reason a still photograph holds attention for twelve seconds instead of two. The map keeps running underneath and is never unmounted — it costs nothing while covered, because paintGround only re-bakes when the camera moves, and a camera under a plate does not move. Under `instant` the drift does not animate: the plate appears already at its end framing, the same discipline as a march that draws itself whole when you seek.

motion.note: Which way the camera drifts. `in` is the push.

focus.note: [x, y] as fractions of the image, what the drift aims at. Default centre, slightly high — faces are rarely in the middle.

over.note: How long the drift takes. Longer than the beat, on purpose: motion you can SEE is motion that distracts.

dim.note: Darken the plate so a caption or quote over it stays readable.

fit.note: How the picture meets a wide stage. `cover` fills it and crops what does not fit, which is right for a painting. `contain` letterboxes, which is the only honest option when the whole frame IS the information: a map, a coin, an inscription. Normally you do not set this -- media.json carries a fit derived from the picture's own shape by tools/fetch-media.py, and this only overrides it.

push.note: How far the camera travels, as a fraction of the frame. Default 0.16, which is what the drift always was. A wide establishing shot wants more; a face wants almost none.

into.note: The cross-dissolve when this plate REPLACES another one that is already up. Default 1.1. Ignored when the plate is coming up over the map, which the whole plate already dissolves for.

over.note: The cross-dissolve back to the map.

fleet.draw.note: Ships, not an arrow. route.draw sizes its arrow by `strength`, which means men per metre of front -- a true statement about an army and a meaningless one about a squadron, where ten destroyers are ten objects in a line. A fleet draws the hulls in line ahead along the travelled part of the track, with wakes trailing, so `over` moves the formation up the fjord and a seek lands it wherever it had got to. The track itself must be water: declare the route `"medium": "sea"` and tools/check-sealanes.py will hold you to it.

ships.note: How many hulls to draw. Capped at eight: past that another lozenge adds nothing and the line stops reading as a line.

kind.note: Sizes the hull and the wake. Not to scale with each other -- at the zoom a fjord is read at a real destroyer is under a pixel.

spacing.note: Pixels between hulls, in line ahead.

summary.en: Take the squadron off the map

fact.show.note: A one-line definition on screen while the word is being said. term.mark makes a word tappable, and almost nobody taps while a voice is running -- so the definition existed and was never seen. This is stage state, shown and hidden by cues, so seeking into the middle of a definition shows the definition. It carries the entry's HOOK, never its body: a fact box is a glance you can read without stopping listening, and the card itself opens the full entry.

kind.note: Which pool the id resolves against, as term.mark.

until.note: How long the box stays up. Default 6.5. The hide is derived from this at compile time against the recorded timing, so it lands the same distance after the spoken word in every language. Authoring the hide on a later BEAT was the previous design and a beat is the wrong unit: a beat can be three sentences.

fact.hide.note: Rarely authored. fact.show derives its own hide from `until`; write this only to take a box down EARLY.
